purpose: Formal adoption record: Emulator commit 722b019 is now the fixed baseline for Choice teacher-data generation. Supersedes choice_semantics_provisional_status_v1_20260724.json's PROVISIONAL label for the same audited choice population - does NOT overwrite it or choice_semantics_baseline_v1_20260724.json (both kept as history, per instruction '旧0d16130は履歴として保持し、上書きしない').

emulator.verification_method: Re-hashed the currently-loaded DLL and re-read git HEAD in C:\STS2_Emulator immediately before this baseline record and again before Choice teacher-data generation; both matched the user-supplied 722b019 values exactly (case-insensitive hash compare).

code.note: unchanged since choice_semantics_baseline_v1_20260724.json - the 722b019 fix required no RL-side rule/code change; CHOICE_TYPE_RULES/lookup/alias table are identical to the 0d16130-era baseline. See 'audit_correction' below for what changed underneath (Emulator-side choiceType mislabel), not on this side.

tests.result: 20/20 passed (unchanged from choice_semantics_baseline_v1_20260724.json - no test changes needed for 722b019 adoption)

reverification_results_summary.determinism: 254/254 choice decisions identical across two independent AFTER runs

audit_correction.summary: The 10 rows the 0d16130-era audit flagged as originValidationStatus=suspected_context_leak (card:GUARDS x6, potion:POWER_POTION x2, potion:SKILL_POTION x2, across scenarios 1934-19/7413-9/7551-16) were NOT a raw origin-context leak. Root cause confirmed via 722b019's diff: Emulator was mislabeling pendingChoice.choiceType as 'GamblingChipDiscard' for these genuinely-unrelated GUARDS/POWER_POTION/SKILL_POTION choices, while origin (originEntityType/originEntityId) was correct all along. RL-side CHOICE_TYPE_RULES's Tier-1 priority trusted that (mislabeled) choiceType and forced an incorrect passthrough/GAMBLING_CHIP result onto what were really GUARDS'/POWER_POTION's/SKILL_POTION's own choices.
audit_correction.resolved_by_722b019: Emulator now reports the correct choiceType for these cases; RL-side CHOICE_TYPE_RULES (unchanged) then naturally falls through to normal origin-based resolution (Tier 2/3), which was already correct.
audit_correction.also_resolved: 3 ToolboxChooseCard rows that had likewise been mislabeled and were relabeled to their correct (non-special) choiceType under 722b019 - same root cause, same fix, no RL-side change required.
audit_correction.old_suspect_10_status_after_722b019: 0 remain Suspect; all 10 correctly re-classified (6 GUARDS + 2 POWER_POTION + 2 SKILL_POTION -> Origin-dependent, resolved via correct origin under the unchanged lookup rules).
audit_correction.not_reclassified_as_valid_by_relabeling_: Gambling Chip's own genuine reset-time null-origin rows (choiceType=GamblingChipDiscard, origin=None, decision_index=0) are unaffected by this fix and remain originValidationStatus=missing - see eligibility note below; this is expected/benign, not a leak.

origin_audit_after_722b019.note: provisional_eligible here is still keyed to the 275-choice Stage B population re-resolved offline against 722b019's corrected facts, not yet the full teacher-data generation population (Choiceデータ生成 section below is a separate, larger extraction).

gambling_chip_reset_null_eligibility.rule: choiceType=GamblingChipDiscard with origin=null is decision_index=0 (Reset-time) is NOT excluded from training eligibility. choiceType alone uniquely determines the meaning (operationMode=passthrough, exceptionEntityKey=relic:GAMBLING_CHIP) independent of origin, per CHOICE_TYPE_RULES's Tier-1 priority. originValidationStatus=missing is tracked for quality-audit visibility only and does not block eligibility for this specific choiceType.
